title: relation/first-cut 0.1.0-draft
description: Two object families: (1) the parsed RELATIONS FILE (TOML, caller-supplied via one or more `--relations FILE` arguments, read as an equivalent JSON structure by tomllib), and (2) one QUERY REPORT of an impact-query tool (`impacted`/`depends`; that tool is not included in this export, but its report shape is documented here). SHAPE vs SEMANTICS: this schema is shape/enum-normative for both; the entity-ref grammar, the relation-vs-propagates cross-field rule, self-loop/duplicate-edge/unresolved-@self detection, and the traversal/determinism rules are cross-field/semantic rules this draft schema does not encode — `tools/relation_vocab.py` checks those (see x-semantic-only-rules).

entity_ref.description: One raw entity-ref string. Minimal shape check (non-empty string); the FULL grammar (repo-id shape, path-segment rules, the whole-repo '**' exception, `@self` forms, `resource:<name>@<host>`) is semantic-only, enforced by tools/relation_vocab.py::parse_entity_ref (see x-semantic-only-rules 'entity-ref-grammar').

relation_token.description: Either a closed_relation, or an x-<token> matching ^x-[a-z0-9-]+$. This schema's `pattern` alternation checks the SHAPE only; tools/relation_vocab.py::is_known_relation / is_x_token is the executable norm.

edge.description: SEMANTIC: `propagates` MUST NOT be present when `relation` is a closed_relation; when `relation` is an x-token, `propagates` is optional and defaults to 'none' at query time when absent. `from`/`to` MUST NOT resolve to the same entity (self-loop). Both cross-field rules are enforced by tools/relation_vocab.py, not by this schema.

relations_file.description: SEMANTIC: no two edges (within this file, or across every --relations file merged into one invocation) may have an identical (from, relation, to, directed, propagates) tuple once every entity-ref is resolved against one --self value — a cross-document rule this draft schema does not encode; tools/relation_vocab.py checks it. An edge using '@self'/'@self:<path>' is invalid unless the invocation supplies --self.

entity.description: canonical (resolved) entity-ref string of the impacted/depended-on entity

hit.description: SEMANTIC: `depth` is the length of the SHORTEST chain that explains this hit; `chain.length == depth` always. `hits[]` as a whole is sorted by (depth, entity) ascending — enforced by tools/relation_vocab.py::traverse, not by this schema.

error_item.description: One diagnostic emitted by a relation tool.

query_report.description: SEMANTIC: every non-ok report, including usage and internal/input failures, has status=='unknown'. For impacted/depends it REQUIRES hits==null AND cycles_detected==null; for cochange it REQUIRES untouched/other_repo/touched==null. status=='ok' carries real result arrays and a boolean cycles_detected. This draft schema does not encode those conditionals; relation_query.py enforces them.

x-semantic-only-rules.description: Every entity-ref (from/to/source, and CLI --changed/--entity values) must satisfy the full grammar: <repo> id shape, no leading '/', no '.'/'..' segment, no empty segment, no backslash/control chars, '*'/'**' disallowed except the whole-repo '<repo>:**' form, resource:<name>@<host> shape, and @self/@self:<path> forms.
An @self/@self:<path> ref only resolves given a --self <repo> value; otherwise it is E_UNRESOLVED_SELF.

contains(a,b): equal; a whole-repo and same repo as b; or a a subtree whose path is a whole-segment prefix of b's path. overlap(a,b) = contains(a,b) or contains(b,a). Used both for self-loop/duplicate detection (equality) and for impact-query matching (overlap).
propagates is invalid on a closed_relation (its direction is the fixed §3 table value); on an x-token it is optional, one of to-from/from-to/none, defaulting to none when absent.
An edge whose from/to resolve to the same canonical entity is invalid, regardless of relation.
Two edges (within one file or across every --relations file in one invocation) with an identical resolved (from, relation, to, directed, propagates) tuple are invalid.

A changed/starting entity matches a propagation edge's source endpoint via OVERLAP (not exact equality); hits[] holds the shortest cycle-safe chain per entity, ties broken by lexicographically smallest chain.
`depends --entity X` runs the identical traversal as `impacted`, with every propagation edge's source/target swapped first — 'walk against propagation'.
If the merged --relations set does not validate, a query report is status=unknown with hits/cycles_detected both null (never an empty array/false) and exit_code = the lowest validation error class.
x-semantic-only-rules.enforced_by: not enforced in this export (the impact-query tool is not included)
